name: Belgian Carbonnade Flamande
description: Carbonnade flamande, Belgium's real beer-and-beef stew, is genuinely thickened with a slice of mustard-spread bread laid on top of the simmering pot, not a roux - the bread dissolves into the sauce as it braises, adding body and a real sharp, tangy note at the same time. Real dark Belgian ale, not wine, is the defining liquid, and the onions are cooked down until genuinely deep brown before anything else goes in.

ingredients_full.note: cup, standing in for dark Belgian ale

ingredients_full.ingredient: 365 (Whole Foods) 365 Everyday Value, White Hamburger Buns

ingredients.note: cup, standing in for dark Belgian ale

ingredients.ingredient: 365 (Whole Foods) 365 Everyday Value, White Hamburger Buns

steps_detailed: Brown the beef in batches, 8-9 minutes, then set aside.
Cook the onion in the same pot over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, 20-25 minutes, until deeply, darkly caramelized - real carbonnade depends on this real depth of color.
Return the beef, add the beer (or wine stand-in), bay leaf, and vinegar.
Spread the bread thickly with mustard and lay it, mustard-side down, directly on top of the stew.
Cover and simmer 1.5-2 hours, until the beef is fall-apart tender and the bread has fully dissolved into the sauce, thickening it naturally.

name: Belgian Moules Marinière
description: Moules marinière, mussels steamed in white wine with shallots and herbs, is Belgium's most iconic dish, real technique steaming just until the shells pop open, since overcooking turns mussels rubbery.

ingredients_full.note: finely minced, standing in for shallot
tbsp, chopped, standing in for parsley

ingredients.note: finely minced, standing in for shallot
tbsp, chopped, standing in for parsley

steps_detailed: Cook the onion and garlic in the butter, 2-3 minutes.
Add the wine and bring to a boil.
Add the mussels, cover tightly, and steam 4-6 minutes, shaking the pot occasionally, until the shells pop open - discard any that stay closed.
Stir in the cilantro just before serving.

name: Belgian Double-Fried Frites
description: Belgian frites are genuinely fried twice at two different temperatures, which is the real technique that separates them from ordinary fries and keeps them crispy long after leaving the oil - a single fry can't achieve the same real crunch.
steps_detailed: Fry the potato batons at a lower temperature, around 325F (163C), for 5-6 minutes, until soft but pale - this first fry cooks the inside through without browning.
Remove and let rest at least 10 minutes.
Fry a second time at a higher temperature, around 375F (190C), for 3-4 minutes, until deeply golden and genuinely crisp - this real second fry is what makes them Belgian frites, not just fries.
Season with salt immediately.

name: Belgian Speculoos-Style Spice Cookies
description: Speculoos, thin, deeply spiced shortbread cookies, are a genuine Belgian classic, real technique using real cinnamon and a warm spice blend for their distinctive character.
steps_detailed: Cream the butter and sugar, then mix in the flour, cinnamon, and cloves into a firm dough.
Roll thin and cut into shapes.
Bake at 350F (175C) for 10-12 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Belgian Endive Gratin
description: Endive gratin, real Belgian endive wrapped in ham and baked with real cheese sauce, is a beloved winter comfort dish, real technique braising the endive first to mellow its natural bitterness.

ingredients_full.note: tbsp, standing in for ham wrap

ingredients.note: tbsp, standing in for ham wrap

steps_detailed: Braise the endive in a little butter and water, covered, 15-18 minutes, until tender and much of its raw bitterness has mellowed.
Top with the cheese and breadcrumbs.
Bake at 375F (190C) for 12-15 minutes until the cheese is melted and golden.

name: Belgian Chocolate Mousse
description: Rich chocolate mousse, reflecting Belgium's world-renowned chocolate tradition, real technique folding whipped egg whites in gently to keep the mousse genuinely light and airy.
steps_detailed: Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar, cocoa, and melted butter until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip the egg whites to stiff peaks.
Gently fold the whites into the chocolate mixture in two additions, keeping as much air in as possible.
Chill at least 2 hours before serving.
